gallery.filename: Possible painting of the pool and temples of the Katas Raj Temple Complex during Sikh-rule, from the 'Gulgashat-i-Punjab', circa 19th century.png
gallery.title: File:Possible painting of the pool and temples of the Katas Raj Temple Complex during Sikh-rule, from the 'Gulgashat-i-Punjab', circa 19th century.png
gallery.credit: Published in the book: 'Maharaja Ranjit Singh: Lord of the Five Rivers' (2002) by Jean-Marie Lafont (in the personal collection of the uploader and relevant pages with the image photographed by them)
gallery.source: Possible painting of the pool and temples of the Katas Raj Temple Complex during Sikh-rule, from the 'Gulgashat-i-Punjab', circa 19th century
gallery.description:
Possible painting of the pool and temples of the Katas Raj Temple Complex (tentatively) during Sikh-rule, from the 'Gulgashat-i-Punjab', circa 19th century. Kept in the collection of the Maharaja Ranjit Singh Museum, Amritsar. Acc. N° 38. The temple complex lays in the Salt Range of Punjab.
This interesting painting showing a pool in a hilly setting with temples around it could well be the Katas and Gandhala in the Salt Range, the famous Jaina and Hindu shrines in Punjab visited and described by Hiuen Tsang in the early 7th century AD The pool was 200 feet long and 150 broad. The "Sat Ghara" or seven temples were attributed to the Pandus, but Cunningham counted no less than twelve temples around the pond and described some of them as being in the Kashmiri style of the Karkota and the Varma dynasties
